memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He humbled you, causing you to hunger and then feeding you with manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to teach you that man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord. - Deut 8:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God allowed Israel to feel hunger in the wilderness, then fed them with manna — a bread they had never seen, appearing fresh each morning like dew. But the lesson went far deeper than filling empty stomachs. God was teaching them that "man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord." Physical food keeps the body alive, but the soul lives on something more — on God Himself and His word.

We are so easily consumed with our physical needs and wants: food, money, comfort, security. These matter, and God provides them. But if we feed only our bodies and starve our souls, we will remain hungry in the deepest place. The manna taught Israel daily dependence — they could not store it up, but had to trust God for fresh provision each morning. In the same way, we need daily nourishment from God's word, not just occasional bites.

These are the very words Jesus used when tempted in His own wilderness. Hungry after forty days of fasting, He answered Satan by quoting this verse (Matt 4:4). Where Israel grumbled in their hunger, Jesus trusted the Father perfectly, showing us the way. And He is Himself "the bread of life" (John 6:35), the true nourishment our souls were made for. Feed your body, yes — but do not neglect the deeper hunger. Let God's word be your daily bread, and find in Christ the satisfaction nothing else can give.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I feeding my body while starving my soul?
- Do I depend on God's word daily, or only occasionally?
- How does Jesus, "the bread of life," satisfy the deepest hunger in me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I so easily focus on physical needs while neglecting my soul. Teach me that I live not on bread alone but on Your word. Let me feed daily on Your truth and find in Jesus the bread of life. Amen.
